title: Jackson, Mississippi with Harry Barth; never played in New York
summary: He spent a year in 1929 with Harry Barth's unsuccessful road band in Jackson and has never played in New York.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: In the 30s, you also went off to New York, right?

I? No. No, no, no. I didn't go to New York then at all. Did you? I went to Jackson, Mississippi in 1929 and spent practically a year up there with Harry Barth, who had a little road band there, very unsuccessful. This was a starvation trip. We had a lot of fun. Harry Barth had played bass with Ted Lewis for years, and he was a Mississippi boy, wanted to come home and start his own band, and it didn't work out, you know. When did you first go to New York? Oh, I didn't get to New York. I've never been to New York as a musician. I've been to New York as a visitor. I went up there a couple of times when I was working on staff at WWL, because they used to take care of the library, physically take care of the library, and we were a CBS affiliate, which they still are, and I'd get up there to try to do things.
